title: WinLean rule
description: A reviewed, declarative WinLean optimization rule. The authoritative validator is src/WinLean.Validation.psm1; this schema provides editor support.

id.description: Lowercase dotted identifier. The first segment is the category prefix, for example 'privacy.advertising-id.disable'. The file must be named <id>.json.

category.description: Rule category. The rule file lives in Rules/<category>/.

description.description: Exactly what the rule changes, including the Windows setting it corresponds to.

rationale.description: Why the change is worth making (its plausible optimization, privacy or usability value).

risk.description: Low: normally safe. Medium: feature-dependent, needs compatibility conditions. High: may affect servicing, security or broad compatibility.

reversible.description: Whether WinLean can restore the previous state. Declarative resources are always reversible.

takesEffect.description: The latest point at which the change is expected to be fully effective.

maxBuild.description: Optional hard upper bound (the setting is known to be gone or changed after this build).

maxValidatedBuild.description: Newest build the rule was validated against. Newer builds require -AllowUntestedBuild.

editions.description: Optional list of EditionID values (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\EditionID) the rule is effective on.

conditions.description: All conditions must be true for the rule to apply. Unknown facts (for example undeclared requirements) skip the rule.

fact.description: requirement.<key> (user compatibility requirement), capability.<key> (detected) or system.<key> (build, editionId, installationType, architecture, displayVersion).

value.description: Boolean for requirements; array for In/NotIn; number for GreaterOrEqual/LessOrEqual.

reason.description: Shown in the plan when the condition is not met.

dependencies.description: Rules that must be applied (or already satisfied) first.

conflicts.description: Rules that must not be applied together with this rule.

sideEffects.description: Possible side effects (write 'None known' only after checking).

notes.description: Additional reviewer notes, for example the Windows default value.

references.description: Sources that document the exact setting (Microsoft documentation, ADMX policy definitions, Microsoft source code).

resources.description: The declarative resources the rule manages. Apply, verify and undo are implemented by the resource provider.

name.description: Value name (the unnamed default value is not supported).

ensure.description: Present (default) sets the value; Absent removes it.

value.description: DWord/QWord: integer; String/ExpandString: string; MultiString: array of strings; Binary: hex string.
